season_storylines: Roughly a third of the league changed schemes this offseason (Stefanski to ATL, Monken to CLE, Kubiak to LV, McCarthy to PIT, John Harbaugh to NYG, Mike LaFleur to ARI, Saleh-Daboll to TEN), and most of the new systems tilt value toward RBs and TEs, which compounds in a non-PPR format where slot WR volume is already devalued.

The QB carousel spun hard: Kyler Murray to MIN, Tua Tagovailoa to ATL, Kirk Cousins to LV, Geno Smith to NYJ, and Murray is winning the Vikings job over J.J. McCarthy (16 of 22 first-team snaps this week), giving him rushing-QB ceiling plus Justin Jefferson in a 6-pt-passing-TD league.

Star WRs relocated en masse (A.J. Brown to NE, DJ Moore to BUF, Jaylen Waddle to DEN, Mike Evans and a returning Deebo Samuel to SF, Stefon Diggs to WAS), so 2025 target trees are unreliable; in this format chase the relocated deep and red-zone roles, not the slot compilers like Diggs.

San Francisco's pass-catching room is in triage: Ricky Pearsall is out for the season after PCL surgery and George Kittle sits on PUP with an Achilles issue (minimum four weeks out if not activated), pushing TD equity to Evans and Deebo and making Jake Tonges a short-term TE stream.

Mike McDaniel landed as Chargers OC and his system historically funnels 21 percent of early-down passes to RBs and 20 percent of targets to TEs, unlocking Justin Herbert's quick game and giving Omarion Hampton a legitimate RB1 path with Ladd McConkey working the middle of the field.
Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs are being tracked as contract hold-ins at camp (verify current practice status), a low-probability but high-impact risk to the two most expensive picks in most drafts.

Miami is in teardown mode after shipping out Tua and Waddle, handing the offense to Malik Willis on a make-or-break deal under new HC Jeff Hafley, and its 4.5 win total says Dolphins skill players face the league's worst scoring environment.

Betting markets frame the season: Baltimore and the Rams top the board at 11.5 wins with a big group (BUF, CIN, DET, KC, NE, PHI, SEA) at 10.5, while Arizona sits at a league-low 3.5, so in a TD-driven format stack the high-total offenses and treat ARI volume as empty calories.
Xavier Worthy re-injured the same shoulder that limited his 2025 season and Kansas City signed Kenneth Walker III, shifting Chiefs TD equity toward the ground game while Worthy's ADP slides.

Preseason games start this week, and they will settle live QB battles in Cleveland (Watson vs Shedeur Sanders), Minnesota, and Atlanta (Penix still not cleared for 11-on-11 in ACL rehab), plus goal-line pecking orders everywhere; the next 72 hours of usage are the most informative of the summer.

teams.outlook: New HC Mike LaFleur imports McVay-tree pace (his offenses ran about 53 plays per game vs Arizona's 45) with heavy motion, but a league-low 3.5 win total and Jacoby Brissett bridging to rookie Carson Beck cap TD output, so treat Cardinals yardage as volume without equity; rookie 1st-rounder Jeremiyah Love headlines the backfield with Tyler Allgeier.

Kevin Stefanski takes over and his Cleveland offenses fed RBs and TEs, so Bijan Robinson (monitor hold-in status) and Kyle Pitts get a scheme boost while Tua Tagovailoa holds the QB job with Michael Penix still rehabbing his ACL and not cleared for 11-on-11.

New HC Jesse Minter is a defensive coach atop a league-high 11.5 win total, and the offense is expected to add more TE-heavy sets, which squeezes Zay Flowers' already-thin target share while keeping the run-and-TD identity that this format pays for.

Joe Brady was promoted to HC and the front office imported DJ Moore from Chicago for a 10.5-win offense, so Buffalo passing TDs stay premium and Ray Davis is a high-value handcuff with return-game upside in a return-yardage league.

Carolina generated almost no verified national camp news this cycle, suggesting staff and scheme continuity rather than upheaval (verify), so price Panthers skill players off last year's roles until preseason usage says otherwise.
Trading DJ Moore to Buffalo vacated a huge target share, and with Luther Burden III (groin) likely missing the preseason, Rome Odunze is positioned as the clear alpha on a 9.5-win offense.
Cincinnati kept its entire core intact at a 10.5 win total, so Burrow-to-Chase TD equity remains elite and Chase Brown's camp buzz points to another every-down workload (verify).

Todd Monken's arrival is a scheme win for RBs and TEs (he featured Chubb and Henry backfields and TE-heavy passing), boosting Quinshon Judkins and Harold Fannin Jr., while the Watson vs Shedeur Sanders battle is live with Monken's snap distribution appearing to favor Sanders.

Dallas is one of the league's most stable situations at 9.5 wins, and the fantasy-relevant camp development is RB Jaydon Blue's explosive-play buzz and rising role, worth a late pick for TD-and-yardage juice.

Denver acquired Jaylen Waddle from Miami (minor leg strain, expected fine within a week) to add field-stretching speed to a 9.5-win offense, and deep-threat roles like his beat slot volume in this scoring.

New playcaller Drew Petzing leans on tight ends, which lifts Sam LaPorta and squeezes Jameson Williams, while newly signed Isiah Pacheco (MCL sprain, expected back for Week 1) is the priority handcuff to Jahmyr Gibbs (monitor Gibbs' hold-in status) on a 10.5-win offense.
Tucker Kraft came off PUP in his ACL comeback with a real shot at Week 1, restoring a TD-dependent TE weapon to a 9.5-win offense; his health is the swing piece of Green Bay's red-zone tree.
Houston replaced the departed Nick Chubb era by trading for David Montgomery, a classic goal-line hammer whose TD role is exactly what this non-PPR format pays for on a 9.5-win team.
Alec Pierce (ankle) is expected off PUP within the week, and his low-catch, high-yardage, deep-ball profile is quietly format-perfect here where 10 yards equals a point and receptions equal nothing.

Year two under Liam Coen has Trevor Lawrence carving up the red zone in camp, Travis Hunter running two-way with real WR usage at a cheap ADP, and a defined committee of Bhayshul Tuten between the 20s, LeQuint Allen on passing downs, and Chris Rodriguez Jr. (foot, says he is ready for Week 1) at the goal line.

Kansas City signed Kenneth Walker III to anchor the ground game at a 10.5 win total while Xavier Worthy re-injured the shoulder that wrecked his 2025, tilting Chiefs TD equity toward the run and making Worthy a falling knife.

Mike McDaniel's OC hire is the scheme upgrade of the offseason: his quick-trigger system historically gives RBs 21 percent of early-down targets and TEs 20 percent of looks, boosting Herbert, Omarion Hampton's RB1 case, Ladd McConkey over the middle, and TE Oronde Gadsden.

The Rams share the league's best win total at 11.5 but lean run-heavy, and Davante Adams at 34 with TD-dependent production and a declining target rate is the classic age-cliff fade even in a TD-friendly format.

New HC Klint Kubiak brings a 12-personnel, RB-friendly scheme with Kirk Cousins named QB1 ahead of rookie Fernando Mendoza, positioning Ashton Jeanty for a featured workload and Brock Bowers for a monster TE route rate, though a 5.5 win total caps the team's TD ceiling.

The Dolphins traded away Tua and Waddle, handed Malik Willis a make-or-break deal under new HC Jeff Hafley with Bobby Slowik calling plays, and carry a 4.5 win total, so treat Miami pass catchers as fade territory and Keaton Mitchell as a cheap explosive-play flier.

Kyler Murray arrived via trade and is seizing the job from J.J. McCarthy (16 of 22 first-team snaps, perfect to Justin Jefferson in recent work), a rushing QB with an elite WR1 in a 6-pt passing TD league; that is a top-tier ceiling combination.

New England imported A.J. Brown from Philadelphia and extended Hunter Henry at a 10.5 win total, while TreVeyon Henderson is pressing Rhamondre Stevenson for early-down and goal-line work; Brown's contested-TD profile travels well in non-PPR.

New Orleans signed Travis Etienne Jr. to lead the backfield and spent a first-rounder on WR Jordyn Tyson, but Tyson's ACL-MCL-PCL history and weak contested-catch rate make him a rookie-hype fade at cost.

John Harbaugh with Matt Nagy calling a 12-and-13-personnel offense favors Theo Johnson and the Cam Skattebo-Tyrone Tracy backfield, while Malik Nabers is practicing and on track for Week 1 in his ACL return, making him a discounted alpha.

Geno Smith arrives with Frank Reich calling plays, and Reich's poor history supporting fantasy RBs plus a three-back committee undercuts Breece Hall on a 5.5-win team, while rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq's hernia setback opens the seam role for Mason Taylor.

New OC Sean Mannion brings heavy pre-snap motion and under-center play-action that attacks the middle of the field, and with A.J. Brown traded to New England the target tree consolidates around Jalen Hurts' rushing TDs, DeVonta Smith, and rookie slot Makai Lemon.

Mike McCarthy's offenses are historically fantasy-friendly, but his West Coast structure trims the downfield throws DK Metcalf needs, and the backfield splits ugly with Rico Dowdle reportedly ahead of Jaylen Warren for goal-line work, which is where this format's RB value lives.

Sam Darnold pilots a 10.5-win offense that lost OC Klint Kubiak to Las Vegas (verify replacement's scheme), and Rashid Shaheed's locked-in kick-return duties plus deep-threat role make him a sneaky double-dip in a return-yardage league.

Brock Purdy's weapons churned overnight: Pearsall is done for the year (PCL), Kittle is on PUP with an Achilles issue (four-plus weeks if not activated), and the team signed Mike Evans and brought back Deebo Samuel, concentrating red-zone targets in two veterans while Jake Tonges streams at TE.

Baker Mayfield enters a contract year off his worst season as a starter, and the backfield is settled with Bucky Irving dominant, Kenneth Gainwell on passing downs (low value in non-PPR), and Sean Tucker buried.

Robert Saleh brought Brian Daboll to call plays, and Daboll's track record lifting QBs makes Cam Ward a cheap 6-pt-TD asset with slot man Chimere Dike and first-round rookie Carnell Tate as the ascending targets.

Stefon Diggs signed on as the primary slot with minimal target competition, but slot catch volume is exactly what this non-PPR format refuses to pay for, and Laremy Tunsil's torn triceps weakens the whole offensive line's floor.

breakout_watch.name: Brock Bowers
breakout_watch.why: Klint Kubiak's Raiders scheme runs 12 personnel at a top-5 rate and his Seattle TE ran a 69 percent route rate, setting Bowers up for elite yardage-and-TD volume that doesn't need receptions to pay off.

breakout_watch.name: Omarion Hampton
breakout_watch.why: Mike McDaniel's system produced consecutive RB5 finishes with De'Von Achane and historically gives RBs 21 percent of early-down passes; Hampton projects toward a top-15 target share among RBs with the rushing role intact, an RB1 path.

breakout_watch.name: Quinshon Judkins
breakout_watch.why: Todd Monken built featured-back workloads for Chubb and Henry, and a Cleveland offense that wants to lean on the run hands Judkins the goal-line-inclusive workhorse role this format pays a premium for.

breakout_watch.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
breakout_watch.why: Monken's scheme has consistently inflated TE production, and Fannin is the seam beneficiary regardless of whether Watson or Shedeur Sanders wins the job.

breakout_watch.name: Kyle Pitts
breakout_watch.why: Kevin Stefanski's offenses made TEs flourish in Cleveland, and pairing Pitts with Tua's quick accuracy is the best scheme-and-QB context of his career at a depressed price.

breakout_watch.name: Ashton Jeanty
breakout_watch.why: Kubiak's RB-friendly, boot-action scheme arrives with a coach who just won a Super Bowl running it, and Jeanty is the unquestioned bell cow; volume plus scheme beats the low team total at his price.

breakout_watch.name: Rome Odunze
breakout_watch.why: The DJ Moore trade vacated a massive target share and Luther Burden III's groin injury clears the preseason runway; Odunze inherits alpha status and the downfield looks that pay in yardage-and-TD scoring.

breakout_watch.name: Bhayshul Tuten
breakout_watch.why: Consistent camp buzz and heavy first-team reps have him leading Jacksonville's committee between the 20s in Liam Coen's offense; if he steals goal-line work from Chris Rodriguez Jr. he is a league-winner.

breakout_watch.name: Travis Hunter
breakout_watch.why: At a WR63 ADP he is showing deep chemistry with a sharp Trevor Lawrence while playing both ways with no injury limitations; the big-play profile fits yardage-and-TD scoring perfectly.

breakout_watch.name: Cam Ward
breakout_watch.why: Brian Daboll just coaxed a top-10 fantasy season out of Daniel Jones and now calls plays for Ward, whose rushing ability plus 6-pt passing TDs gives him sneaky QB1 upside at a late-round cost.

breakout_watch.name: Mason Taylor
breakout_watch.why: Rookie first-rounder Kenyon Sadiq's hernia setback hands Taylor the Jets' seam role with Geno Smith, a veteran who has historically fed the intermediate middle.

breakout_watch.name: Jaydon Blue
breakout_watch.why: Explosive camp plays and positive coaching feedback have moved him up 15-plus ADP spots in Dallas's stable offense; his home-run speed is pure yardage-league upside.

breakout_watch.name: Zachariah Branch
breakout_watch.why: Atlanta ranked last in kick-return average and imported a returner with both a punt and kick return TD in college; in a league paying return yards plus 6-pt return TDs, his special-teams role alone is startable-adjacent depth.

breakout_watch.name: Malik Washington
breakout_watch.why: A live path to the Raiders' WR1 role stacked on kick-return duties gives him two scoring avenues in a return-yardage league at essentially free cost (verify camp usage this week).

fade_watch.name: Christian McCaffrey
fade_watch.why: Age 30 coming off 450-plus touches is the exact workload-cliff profile that craters, and his price still assumes the ceiling; the downside case is season-wrecking at his ADP.

fade_watch.name: Breece Hall
fade_watch.why: Frank Reich's poor history supporting fantasy RBs plus a three-back committee on a 5.5-win offense guts both his volume and his TD equity.

fade_watch.name: Davante Adams
fade_watch.why: Age 34 with nearly 38 percent of his scoring from TDs, a declining target rate, and a run-leaning Rams offense is a textbook TD-regression and age-cliff stack.

fade_watch.name: Zay Flowers
fade_watch.why: A sub-7 target-per-game share is set to shrink further as Baltimore adds more TE-heavy sets under the new staff; low volume without a TD role has no floor in this format.

fade_watch.name: Jameson Williams
fade_watch.why: New playcaller Drew Petzing tilts targets to tight ends, and behind St. Brown and LaPorta the deep-shot-only role means boom-bust weeks with a fading TD share.

fade_watch.name: DK Metcalf
fade_watch.why: McCarthy's West Coast structure limits the downfield throws that made Metcalf valuable, and a deep threat without deep targets is just an expensive decoy.

fade_watch.name: Jaylen Warren
fade_watch.why: Rico Dowdle is reportedly the superior goal-line back in Pittsburgh's split, and in a league where goal-line roles are gold, Warren is the half of the committee this scoring punishes.

fade_watch.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
fade_watch.why: His 2025 line was inflated by three soft matchups, TreVeyon Henderson is pressing for early-down and goal-line work, and the schedule stiffens.

fade_watch.name: Xavier Worthy
fade_watch.why: He re-injured the same shoulder that limited all of 2025 and Kansas City just paid Kenneth Walker III, pointing Chiefs red-zone equity away from him.

fade_watch.name: Jordyn Tyson
fade_watch.why: A first-round pedigree can't offset an ACL-MCL-PCL history, a 44 percent contested-catch rate, and limited YAC; rookie-WR hype at his price is the classic August trap.

uncertainty_note: The most unsettled situations right now: three live QB battles (Minnesota's Murray-McCarthy job is trending but not official, Cleveland's Watson-Sanders snaps conflict with beat predictions, and Atlanta hinges on Penix's ACL clearance), the Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs contract hold-ins whose practice status could shift daily, San Francisco's Kittle PUP decision (activation vs a four-plus-week absence changes the TE market), and several fresh soft-tissue injuries (Burden, Worthy, Waddle) whose timelines are camp-speak until preseason games start this week; some relocated-player details above rest on single-source camp reporting, so re-verify roles marked (verify) before drafting.
